title: A saturated auxiliary reference realizes finite resolvent filters
statement: For the stated finite-dimensional saturated auxiliary-reference construction, the denominator entropy Hessian is an exact weighted resolvent integral and every finite simple-resolvent sum is realizable; a normalized concentrating family recovers the SLD kernel. The N966 receiving application has additional reference-marginal and zero-reference-tangent conditions stated in the contract.

requires: Finite-dimensional channels and a faithful baseline with a Hermitian tangent; each perturbation parameter is sufficiently small for faithfulness.
For the N966 receiving necessity argument, H_R=0 on the original reference so that its marginal is independent of the perturbation.
A saturated auxiliary pair with a centre and finitely many leaves; every finite resolvent filter uses a finite auxiliary space.
provides: An exact denominator Hessian as a weighted resolvent integral for the stated saturated pair.
A finite realization of every finite simple-resolvent sum and a normalized concentrating family yielding the SLD kernel.
assumptions: The N966 receiving pair has reference marginals sigma_R tensor tau and sigma_R tensor W/Z, which are intentionally different.
At epsilon=0 the conditional deficits vanish, enabling baseline subtraction for the receiving comparison at arbitrary finite c.
The raw common relative-entropy baseline also cancels in the special case c=1; this does not make the reference marginals equal.
The filter-order limit is taken after the finite-stage Hessian comparison.
costs: Auxiliary reference dimension and finite residues can grow with filter order; large coefficients reduce the admissible perturbation interval.
No uniform lower bound on that interval, conditioning bound, or precision guarantee is established.
contract.units: Finite-dimensional relative-entropy Hessian / SLD metric coefficient.
contract.obstruction: If equal marginals are imposed in the specified centre-and-leaf construction, H_R=0 forces tau=W/Tr(W), removing the coherent cross-leaf terms needed by its signed-residue filter. This obstructs that compiler architecture, not every positive realization or every different construction. The receiving proof establishes a conditional statement, not complete equal-reference Umegaki realization for arbitrary quantum channels.

body: Receiving use in N966 is narrower than the finite-filter identity: the necessity argument tests only tangents with H_R=0 and uses the saturated pair with different reference marginals. At epsilon=0 the conditional deficits vanish, which permits the Hessian comparison for arbitrary c; the raw common baseline also cancels when c=1. Equalizing the marginals destroys this specific coherent filter localization.
